To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a novel chemical series of potent microsomal prostlandin E synthetase-1 inhibitors, which were designed to inhibit prostlandin E2 biosynthesis, induced kidney toxicity in a rat toxicity study.

the kidney toxicity of a new mPGES-2 inhibitor was related to amide hydrolytic metabolite (determinded M1), and that a new and active compound with reduced propensity to undergo hydrolysis has been identified.

a new mPGES- 1 inhibitor was identified with improved margins to kidney toxicity in rats by including metabolic profiling, and that a working hypothesis was generated to explain the kidney toxicity of a novel mPGES- -1 inhibitor in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of novel chemical series of microsomal prostglandin E synthases (mPGES) inhibitors and the development of a novel chemical series of mPGES inhibitors.
the discovery and development of a new chemical entity (NCE) for the treatment of pain, inflammation and fever.
the development of a new chemical series of mPGES- 1 inhibitors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the kidney toxicity seen in the 7-day toxicity rat study with compound 1 was caused by a metabolite (M1), formed via amide hydrolytic cleavage, which is a well-recognized metabolic pathway for amide-containing compounds.
a novel microsomal PGES-1 inhibitor induced kidney injury in rats at exposures representing less that 4 times the efficacious exposure in rats.

a novel mPGES- 1 inhibitor with improved pharmacological properties and improved margins to kidney toxicity was identified by including metabolic profiling, exploratory rat toxicity, and in vitro hepatocyte metabolism studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the amide hydrolytic pathway for a novel chemical series of mPGES- 1 inhibitors was identified as a potential source of kidney toxicity in rats and was successfully mitigated.
a novel mPGES- 1 inhibitor with an acceptable safety profile in man has been identified.
the use of metabolic profiling and in vivo toxicity studies can help guide the selection of a chemical series for further development and can help to avoid the risk of inducing toxicity in man.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the kidney should not be overlooked when conducting exploratory toxicology studies with new drug candidates, and that metabolic profiling can be useful to identify potential toxic metabolites and guide the development of new drug candidates.
amide hydrolytic metabolites of mPGES- 1 inhibitors should be considered when evaluating the potential risk of inducing kidney injury in rat toxicology studies.
metabolic profiling can be a useful tool to guide the design of new chemical entities and to avoid the risk of inducing chemically mediated toxicity.
